title: ENFORCEMENT RULES OF THE HOUSING BENEFITS ACT
full_text:
Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of these Rules is to prescribe matters delegated by the Housing Benefits Act and the Enforcement Decree of that Act, and matters necessary for their enforcement.

Article 2 (Measures upon Change of Residence, etc.)
Article 33 of the Enforcement Rules of the National Basic Living Security Act shall govern the measures to be taken when an eligible recipient or recipient changes residence and cooperation among housing security agencies under Article 6(2) of the Housing Benefits Act (hereinafter referred to as the "Act").

Article 3 (Administration of Housing Benefits)
(1) Housing benefits shall be provided on the basis of individual households under subparagraph 8 of Article 2 of the National Basic Living Security Act. <Amended on April 20, 2015>

(2) Where housing benefits are provided regularly in cash, they shall be paid on the 20th day of each month (or the preceding day if the 20th is a Saturday or public holiday).

(3) Where housing benefits are first provided to a person determined to be a recipient under Article 26 of the National Basic Living Security Act, the full housing benefits for the month in which the benefits commence shall be provided.

(4) Where an eligible recipient or recipient changes residence under Article 6(2) of the Act and reports the move under the Resident Registration Act, housing benefits for the month in which the move-in date falls (meaning the housing benefits applicable in the area of the relevant housing security agency) shall be provided by the housing security agency determined as follows:
1. If the move-in date is on or before the 15th: The Special Self-Governing City Mayor, Special Self-Governing Province Governor, or head of a Si/Gun/Gu (hereinafter referred to as the "head of a Si/Gun/Gu") having jurisdiction over the new residence;
2. If the move-in date is on or after the 16th: The head of a Si/Gun/Gu having jurisdiction over the former residence.

(5) Where a lease contract concluded by a recipient changes, housing benefits for the month in which the contract changes shall be provided as follows:
1. If the change takes place on or before the 15th: Housing benefits under the new lease contract;
2. If the change takes place on or after the 16th: Housing benefits under the former lease contract.

(6) Where a recipient falls under either of the following, the full housing benefits for the month in which the relevant event occurs shall be provided:
1. Housing benefits are suspended on a ground specified in a subparagraph of Article 14(2) of the Act or a subparagraph of Article 30(1) of the National Basic Living Security Act;
2. The recipient dies: Provided, That this shall not apply if there is no other recipient in the deceased recipient's household.

(7) For a recipient who enters or leaves a facility specified by the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport, such as a security facility under Article 32 of the National Basic Living Security Act, housing benefits for the month in which the date of entry or departure falls shall be provided as follows: <Amended on April 20, 2015>
1. Entry on or before the 15th: 50 percent of the housing benefits for that month;
2. Entry on or after the 16th: The full housing benefits for that month;
3. Departure on or before the 15th: The full housing benefits for that month;
4. Departure on or after the 16th: 50 percent of the housing benefits for that month.

Article 4 (Receipt of Rent on Behalf of a Recipient, etc.)
(1) "Unavoidable reasons prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport" in the proviso of Article 7(4) of the Act means cases where the recipient falls under any subparagraph of Article 6(1) of the Enforcement Decree of the National Basic Living Security Act.

(2) Where a recipient falls under a reason referred to in paragraph (1), rent may be paid into an account in the name of the recipient's spouse, lineal blood relative, or collateral blood relative within the third degree of kinship (hereinafter referred to as a "spouse or relative").

(3) A spouse or relative shall submit to the head of a Si/Gun/Gu an application for receipt of housing benefits on behalf of a recipient in attached Form 1 (including an application in electronic form), together with the following documents (including electronic documents):
1. A document enabling verification of the recipient's personal particulars;
2. A document proving that a reason under paragraph (1) applies;
3. A document enabling verification that the person is a spouse or relative.

(4) Before paying rent into an account in the name of a spouse or relative under paragraph (2), the head of a Si/Gun/Gu shall inform the spouse or relative of the following:
1. The reason for payment;
2. The purpose for which the rent is to be used;
3. Matters concerning the prohibition on using the rent for other purposes and related matters.

(5) If the recipient or spouse or relative resides in an area without a financial company or post office, or if another unavoidable reason exists, such as a disruption of information and communications services, the rent may be paid directly to the recipient or spouse or relative.

Article 5 (Receipt of Repair and Maintenance Expenses on Behalf of a Recipient, etc.)
(1) "Unavoidable reasons prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport" in the proviso of Article 8(3) of the Act means cases where the recipient falls under Article 4(1).

(2) Where an unavoidable reason under paragraph (1) exists, Article 4(2) through (5) shall apply mutatis mutandis to the method of paying repair and maintenance expenses under subparagraph 1 of Article 2 of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "repair and maintenance expenses").

Article 6 (Method of Providing Repair and Maintenance Expenses, etc.)
(1) Repair and maintenance expenses shall be provided by carrying out the repairs necessary to maintain the housing, etc. in which the recipient resides.

(2) The head of a Si/Gun/Gu shall establish an annual repair plan after conducting investigations on applications and investigations for verification under Articles 10 and 11 of the Act.

(3) The head of a Si/Gun/Gu shall carry out repairs in accordance with the annual repair plan under paragraph (2), and shall obtain the recipient's consent before carrying out the repairs.

(4) Notwithstanding paragraphs (2) and (3), if the head of a Si/Gun/Gu considers urgent repairs necessary, the head may, with the recipient's consent, carry out repairs without establishing an annual repair plan or separately from the annual repair plan.

(5) The head of a Si/Gun/Gu may request an institution specified by the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport to establish an annual repair plan, carry out repairs, and perform related tasks under paragraphs (2) through (4).

(6) Matters necessary for establishing annual repair plans, the scope and methods of repairs, repair cycles, and other related matters, other than those prescribed in paragraphs (1) through (5), shall be determined by the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport.

Article 7 (Investigations on Applications)
(1) "Matters prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport" in Article 10(1)2 of the Act means the following:
1. Whether the rent is appropriate;
2. The current conditions of the housing, etc., including its type and the state of its facilities;
3. Whether the person actually resides there;
4. Other matters necessary for paying rent that are specified by the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport.

(2) "Matters prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport" in Article 10(2)2 of the Act means the following:
1. Rights relating to the housing, etc.;
2. Recent repair and maintenance history;
3. Whether the person actually resides there;
4. Other matters necessary for paying repair and maintenance expenses that are specified by the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport.

Article 8 (Investigations for Verification)
"Matters prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport" in Article 11(1)3 of the Act means the following:
1. The matters specified in each subparagraph of Article 7(1) and (2);
2. Whether monthly rent referred to in Article 14(2)2 of the Act is in arrears;
3. Other matters necessary for providing housing benefits that are specified by the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport.

Article 9 (Methods and Procedures of Investigation, etc.)
(1) "Materials prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport, such as materials proving a lease contract" in Article 13(1) of the Act means the following:
1. Materials proving a lease contract;
2. Materials necessary to investigate the matters specified in the subparagraphs of Article 8.

(2) When the head of a Si/Gun/Gu or an institution requested to conduct investigations on applications and investigations for verification under Article 12(1) of the Act requires submission of materials listed in paragraph (1), the head or institution shall require only the minimum materials necessary for those investigations.

(3) The identification card indicating the authority of a person conducting investigations on applications and investigations for verification under Article 13(2) of the Act shall be in attached Form 2.

Article 10 (Suspension and Resumption of Housing Benefits)
(1) "Period prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport" in Article 14(2)2 of the Act means 3 months. In this case, rent arrears shall be limited to those arising during the term of the lease contract applicable at the time of the decision to suspend housing benefits.

(2) A lessor who wishes to apply to receive monthly rent directly under Article 4(3)2(b) of the Enforcement Decree of the Housing Benefits Act (hereinafter referred to as the "Decree") shall submit an application for direct receipt of monthly rent in attached Form 1, together with the following documents:
1. The lease contract;
2. A document enabling verification that the person is the lessor;
3. A document proving the recipient's agreement and consent under Article 4(3)2(b) of the Decree.

(3) Where housing benefits are provided to a lessor under Article 4(3)2(b) of the Decree and paragraph (2) of this Article, they shall be paid into an account in the lessor's name: Provided, That if the lessor resides in an area without a financial company or post office, or if another unavoidable reason exists, such as a disruption of information and communications services, the rent may be paid directly to the lessor.

Article 11 (Computerization of Housing Benefit Payment Affairs)
"Materials prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport" in Article 17(3)5 of the Act means the following: <Amended on December 29, 2015>
1. Materials necessary for paying rent and repair and maintenance expenses that are included in the rental housing information system under Article 60 of the Special Act on Private Rental Housing;
2. Materials necessary for paying rent and repair and maintenance expenses that are included in the information system under Article 6-2 of the Social Welfare Services Act;
3. Materials necessary for paying rent and repair and maintenance expenses that are included in the computerized information processing system under Article 3-6 of the Housing Lease Protection Act;
4. Materials concerning housing benefit costs borne by local governments under Article 19 of the Act;
5. Other materials necessary for paying rent and repair and maintenance expenses that are specified by the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport.

ADDENDA <Ordinance No. 126, September 30, 2014>

Article 1 (Enforcement Date)
These Rules shall enter into force on October 1, 2014: Provided, That Articles 5 and 6 shall enter into force on January 1, 2015.

Article 2 (Starting Date for Calculating Monthly Rent Arrears Constituting a Ground for Suspension of Housing Benefits)
The 3-month period of rent arrears under Article 10(1) shall be calculated from the date publicly notified by the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport, taking into account the timing of the transfer of housing benefit affairs under the National Basic Living Security Act.

ADDENDA (Enforcement Rules of the National Basic Living Security Act) <Ordinance No. 309, April 20, 2015>

Article 1 (Enforcement Date)
These Rules shall enter into force on July 1, 2015.

Article 2 (Amendment of Other Statutes)
The Enforcement Rules of the Housing Benefits Act shall be partially amended as follows:
In Article 3(1), "subparagraph 7 of Article 2 of the National Basic Living Security Act" shall be replaced by "subparagraph 8 of Article 2 of the National Basic Living Security Act"; and in the part of paragraph (7) of that Article preceding the subparagraphs, "Article 38 of the Enforcement Decree of the National Basic Living Security Act" shall be replaced by "Article 32 of the National Basic Living Security Act".

ADDENDA (Enforcement Rules of the Special Act on Private Rental Housing) <Ordinance No. 270, December 29, 2015>

Article 1 (Enforcement Date)
These Rules shall enter into force on the date of their promulgation.

Articles 2 through 4 Omitted.

Article 5 (Amendment of Other Statutes)
(1) and (2) Omitted.
(3) The Enforcement Rules of the Housing Benefits Act shall be partially amended as follows:
In subparagraph 1 of Article 11, "Article 20-7 of the Rental Housing Act" shall be replaced by "Article 60 of the Special Act on Private Rental Housing".

Article 6 Omitted.

Amendment Text

⊙ Ordinance of the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport No. 270 (December 29, 2015)

Ordinance Wholly Amending the Enforcement Rules of the Rental Housing Act

The Enforcement Rules of the Rental Housing Act shall be wholly amended as follows.

ENFORCEMENT RULES OF THE SPECIAL ACT ON PRIVATE RENTAL HOUSING

[Main text omitted]

ADDENDA

Article 1 (Enforcement Date)
These Rules shall enter into force on the date of their promulgation.

Articles 2 through 4 Omitted.

Article 5 (Amendment of Other Statutes)
(1) and (2) Omitted.
(3) The Enforcement Rules of the Housing Benefits Act shall be partially amended as follows:
In subparagraph 1 of Article 11, "Article 20-7 of the Rental Housing Act" shall be replaced by "Article 60 of the Special Act on Private Rental Housing".

Article 6 Omitted.

Grounds for Enactment and Amendment

[Whole Amendment]

◇ Grounds for Amendment
The Rental Housing Act and its Enforcement Decree, which focused on regulation and comprehensive management of both public and private rental housing, have been wholly amended into the Special Act on Private Rental Housing (Act No. 13499, promulgated on August 28, 2015 and effective on December 29, 2015) and its Enforcement Decree (Presidential Decree No. 26763, promulgated on December 28, 2015 and effective on December 29, 2015), which focus on support for private rental housing. Accordingly, these Rules prescribe matters delegated by the Act and Presidential Decree and matters necessary for their enforcement, including procedures for registering and deregistering private rental housing business operators, procedures for proposing the designation of promotion zones for the supply of enterprise-type rental housing and methods of calculating the area of land for which consent has been obtained, and rent conversion rates.

◇ Main Content

(a) Procedures for registration of rental business operators and reporting changes (draft Articles 2 and 3)
Documents to be submitted when registering a rental business operator are specified for each type of operator, including persons who own housing and persons who intend to acquire housing. Extensions of 10 percent or less that remain within the relevant private rental housing size category are excluded from the requirement to report changes.

(b) Preliminary basic investigations of promotion zones and proposal procedures (draft Articles 9 and 10)
1) A person intending to propose the designation of a promotion zone for the supply of enterprise-type rental housing is to investigate matters such as the area's population, transportation, and environment and prepare a preliminary basic investigation report. Where necessary for the investigation, the person may request cooperation from public institutions and other relevant bodies.
2) A person intending to propose designation of a promotion zone is to submit documents and drawings, including an outline business plan and preliminary basic investigation report, to the designating authority. Upon receiving a proposal for designation of a promotion zone, the designating authority is to decide whether to accept the proposal following on-site investigation and other relevant steps, and notify the proposer.

(c) Method of calculating the area of land for which consent has been obtained (draft Article 11)
1) For the purpose of proposing designation of a promotion zone, where land is co-owned, one representative co-owner is deemed the owner of that land, and that representative's consent is counted as consent for the entire area of the land. Where a superficies has been established over land, the consent of the superficies holder and that of the owner are each counted as consent for land corresponding to one half of the area of the land. These and other methods of calculating the area for which consent has been obtained are prescribed.
2) A person who has consented to designation of a promotion zone may withdraw that consent by content-certified mail before the proposer submits the proposal to the designating authority.

(d) Rent conversion rate (draft Article 18)
When converting a rental deposit into monthly rent or monthly rent into a rental deposit, the conversion rate must not exceed the rate applied under Article 7-2 of the Housing Lease Protection Act.

<Provided by the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport>

review_notes: Direct translation of exact Korean source kr-012149-178495-ko and held XML. Fresh family/source_version query found zero existing non-Korean translations and no registered family or edition.

Article 3 thresholds include day 15 and day 16, with distinct relocation, contract-change, entry and departure consequences. The regular-payment exception says preceding day, not an added preceding-business-day rule.
Article 3 death exception preserves full-month entitlement only where another recipient remains in the household. Emergency repair in Article 6 still requires recipient consent.
Article 4 lineal relatives or collateral blood relatives within degree 3 preserved, together with proxy-receipt conditions, attachments, advance notices and direct-cash exceptions.
Historical limited/full incapacity terminology in Form 1 preserved as judicial status; not silently converted into a modern guardianship requirement.
